faq_ci_a: Yes. Create a project token and call the sync endpoint from your pipeline, for example after a release. You can poll the run until it is done.
faq_ci_q: Can I trigger a sync from CI?
faq_data_a: Your data is only visible to members of your workspace. We use no tracking or analytics. The privacy statement lists every service provider involved.
faq_data_q: Where is my data and who can see it?
faq_format_a: No. wortwerk reads JSON (nested, flat or i18next style), Rails YAML and gettext PO files as they are, and writes them back with the same key order, nesting and comments.
faq_format_q: Do I have to change my translation files?
faq_keys_a: One source string, no matter how many languages it is translated into. A message with plural forms counts as a single key.
faq_main_a: Never. Translations go to a dedicated branch (wortwerk/translations by default) and reach your main branch only through a pull request you review and merge.
faq_main_q: Will wortwerk push to my main branch?
faq_mt_a: On the Project and Agency plans you can pre-translate a whole project or a single key with AI. Placeholders and plural forms are checked, and every machine translation is marked for review.
faq_providers_a: GitHub (through a GitHub App) and Bitbucket Cloud. For anything else you can upload files manually or trigger syncs from CI with a project token.
faq_removed_a: The key is marked obsolete and its translations are kept. If the key comes back, everything is restored. Obsolete keys are only purged when you decide to.
faq_removed_q: What happens when I delete a key in my code?
faq_subtitle: The short answers to what teams usually ask first.
